newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest barley, wheat prices rise on bad weather.
newsitem.headline: Budapest barley, wheat prices rise on bad weather.

text.p: Milling wheat and barley futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) rose on Wednesday due to ongoing position-closing induced by fears of low-quality crops, traders said.
"Most selling positions (of wheat) are speculative and current rains do not favour the wheat harvest," said Varga Gyorgy of OTP Forex.
He added that an overnight rise in Chicago wheat prices reinforced the current rising trend on the BCE.
Milling wheat futures rose by between 300 and 400 forints per tonne to finish at 20,700 forints for August, 22,170 for December and 24,300 for May, respectively.
Barley prices, which went up by the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all maturities, were also driven by bad weather that delays harvesting, Varga said.
Barley prices finished at between 17,600 for August and 21,300 forints for May.
Maize futures remained trendless and traded only in small volumes in the absence of fresh news.
Maize prices remained flat for all maturities but December which rose 50 forints to 19,000 and July 1998 which closed at 21,930, down 70.
Total grains turnover jumped to 955 lots or 415.9 million forints from Tuesday's 723 lots or 287.7 million forints.
